newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Shell says '97 margins under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Shell says '97 margins under pressure.

text.p: Shell Refining Co (FOM) Bhd chairman Megat Zaharuddin Nor said on Thursday that refining margins will remain under pressure this year.
"Profitability...will remain heavily dependent upon refining margins that will be exposed to a likely overhang of surplus refining capacity in the Asian region," he said.
"First quarter margins were lower than what we saw over last whole year," Megat Zaharuddin said.
He was speaking at the annual meeting of Shell.
Speaking to reporters later, Megat said the company has moved to raise efficiency.
"Profits will also be under pressure but we have put in some efficiency measures" over the last eight years.
He said the company also has a mix of products which allows it to achieve higher profitability despite a squeeze on margins.
But he declined to comment on profit expectations for the current year.
Commenting on crude prices, he said: "It is a bit surprising that prices are as high as they are. We expect them to come down a bit...pretty soon."
The scenario should become clearer by June, he said.
On the reduction of the stake in Shell Refining by Royal Dutch/Shell Group, Megat said it will be effected through a private placement.
The Malaysian government's licensing conditions for a Shell Refining capacity increase was tied to the Anglo-Dutch group reducing its stake from 75 percent to 60 percent in its Malaysian unit.

He said 10 percent of the total equity was being sold to Bumiputra (ethnic Malay) shareholders and the remaining to other Malaysians. He indicated that the new holders of the 15 percent equity in the company would be less than 10 in number.
